flask-01.notes: Both ground-truth files retrieved (recall 1.0), but the top of the ranked list is dominated by unrelated entities literally named 'application' (a test variable, a WSGI callable variable) that outrank the actual Flask class (src.flask.app.Flask lands at rank 7 of 10). A consumer reading only the top 2-3 results would miss the real answer. Root cause: TF-IDF cosine similarity favors very short documents (a 1-token entity whose entire indexed text is just its own name scores a perfect 1.0 term-frequency on that token) over the actual Flask class, whose large lexical_representation dilutes the same token's relative weight.

flask-02.notes: SessionInterface and SecureCookieSessionInterface both retrieved within the top 6; a downstream consumer would land on the correct answer here.

flask-03.notes: Complete miss -- src/flask/wrappers.py (the Request class) never appears in the top 10 despite being the unambiguous, single-file answer. Retrieved entities (Flask, Scaffold, App, View, AppContext, SessionInterface) are all real and loosely topically adjacent but none answer the question. No fabrication, but the correct answer is simply absent from what a consumer would see.

flask-04.notes: Best-performing relationship query: Scaffold.route, Scaffold.add_url_rule, and the Scaffold/App classes are all retrieved with recall 1.0 and the best precision (0.4) of any answerable query. Correctly supports the two-hop route()->add_url_rule() chain.

flask-05.notes: PHASE B RESULT: the 0.25 confidence threshold cut Blueprint.record (sansio/blueprints.py), the one entity that gave the baseline run partial file-level recall -- its TF-IDF score fell below the bar. What remains (App.register_blueprint, blueprint-named test variables) no longer touches sansio/blueprints.py or blueprints.py at all: recall 0.5 -> 0.0, verdict PARTIAL -> FALSE. This is the predicted, documented cost of thresholding an unfixed score (see context.py's Phase B docstring): the calibration data showed real matches and noise overlap almost completely in this score range, so a threshold that cuts noise inevitably cuts some real matches with it. Expected to improve once Phase D corrects the underlying score.

flask-06.notes: File-level recall shows 1.0 (app.py appears) but this is misleading for a multi-hop query: of the 5 methods the ground truth names (wsgi_app, full_dispatch_request, preprocess_request, dispatch_request, finalize_request), only dispatch_request is actually retrieved -- and even that ranks below several irrelevant test-file 'dispatch_request'/'end_of_request' hits from unrelated test classes. wsgi_app, full_dispatch_request, preprocess_request, and finalize_request are all absent from the top 10. This is exactly the case the benchmark spec calls out: a shallow retrieval that surfaces only one of several needed methods should not be scored as fully correct, and file-level recall alone would have hidden this failure.

flask-07.notes: PHASE B RESULT: SessionInterface and SecureCookieSessionInterface (the baseline run's partial-credit evidence) both fell below the 0.25 threshold. Only one weak match survives (a test function whose name happens to contain 'session'/'cookies'). Verdict PARTIAL -> FALSE, same root cause and same expected resolution as flask-05.

flask-08.notes: Complete miss -- Flask.run() (app.py:633) never retrieved. Instead dominated by test-file variables literally named 'called' and 'debug' from entirely unrelated tests, again consistent with the short-document TF-IDF bias: a variable whose entire indexed text is one token ('called') scores higher than the real run() method's diluted term weights.

flask-09.notes: sansio/app.py retrieved via App.url_rule_class (a tangential Variable), but the actual answer method, App.raise_routing_exception, is absent from the top 10 -- it only appears in 'unknowns'. Right file, wrong entity.

flask-10.phase_b_change: verdict unchanged (was already FALSE at baseline)
flask-10.notes: PHASE B RESULT: verdict unchanged -- was already FALSE at baseline (handle_user_exception/handle_exception were never retrieved even before thresholding, only visible via 'unknowns'). The threshold now cuts jsonify/send_from_directory/View/App too, leaving only make_response (0.252, barely above the 0.25 bar) -- less noise, but the underlying wrong-methods problem this threshold cannot fix is unchanged. File-level recall dropped 1.0 -> 0.0 as a side effect, but that never reflected real correctness here to begin with (see original PARTIAL-looking-but-actually-FALSE note).

flask-11.notes: Complete miss -- FlaskClient/EnvironBuilder (testing.py) never retrieved. Dominated by unrelated test-file local variables literally named 'test_client', the same short-document TF-IDF pattern as flask-08/flask-03.

flask-12.notes: Strongest cross-file result: App.register_blueprint, Blueprint.register_blueprint, the Blueprint class, and BlueprintSetupState (+ its __init__) are all retrieved, correctly spanning both files. Missing the specific Blueprint.register (sansio/blueprints.py:273) and BlueprintSetupState.add_url_rule (line 87) methods that complete the exact chain, so scored PARTIAL rather than fully correct, but this is the best multi-hop/cross-file result in the Flask set.

flask-13.phase_b_change: IMPROVED but not fixed (10 noisy entities -> 1, still not insufficient_evidence)
flask-13.notes: PHASE B RESULT: the threshold cut DebugFilesKeyError and 8 other results, leaving only Request.max_form_parts's local variable (score 0.286, just above the bar) -- real noise reduction, but insufficient_evidence is still False (something cleared the threshold), so this is not yet a full fix. Original baseline finding (no relevance signal at all) is the direct cause; Phase H's fuller existence-query taxonomy is the next step for cases like this where a lone weak match survives thresholding.

flask-14.notes: PHASE B RESULT: a genuine fix. examples/tutorial/flaskr/db.py's get_db() (the baseline's false-premise risk) fell below the 0.25 threshold along with everything else; zero entities survive and RetrievedContext.insufficient_evidence / GroundingContext.insufficient_evidence are both True, with the disclaimer explicitly prefixed 'NO_SUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE'. This is the first negative query in the whole benchmark to be handled correctly.
